index.subtitulo: Automation panel to configure, optimize and customize your Fedora Linux quickly and safely.
index.card_guiado_desc: Follow the Fedora configuration sessions step by step, in the right order — the order matters for the end result, so this is the only way to go through them.
index.card_manut_desc: Everyday tasks that don't depend on order: manage kernels, clean temporary files, adjust GRUB, update or uninstall FOF.
index.card_manut_feat4: Update, uninstall and view FOF changelog
index.sobre_texto: FOF is an open-source tool that automates the main Fedora Linux setup tasks, from installing codecs and repositories to optimizing the system and managing kernels.
index.dica1: Progress of each action saved automatically on the local server
index.dica2: State of each action saved automatically, without relying on reports
index.dica5: Global search (Ctrl+K) to find any session or button
index.dica6: Support for GNOME, KDE, XFCE and more
index.footer_creditos: Fedora Only Fans — Made with ❤️ by VitãoTub
index.footer_legal: Fedora is a registered trademark of Red Hat, Inc. This project is not affiliated with Red Hat.

manutencao.descricao: Standalone tasks that don't depend on order: system cleanup, kernel management, GRUB configuration, update, uninstall and FOF changelog.

00-boas-vindas.sobre_o_que: Fedora Only Fans (FOF) is a visual automation panel for setting up Fedora Linux. It brings together, in a friendly interface, the steps that would normally require terminal commands — from the initial system tuning to getting everything ready for daily use and gaming.
00-boas-vindas.sobre_porque: Fedora is excellent, but it requires some initial steps (enabling RPM Fusion, installing codecs, configuring drivers) that often intimidate users coming from distributions like Ubuntu, Linux Mint or Zorin OS. FOF automates those steps and presents them clearly, in guided sessions — without you having to remember commands or search for tutorials.
00-boas-vindas.sobre_ganhos: With FOF, you get your Fedora complete in a few clicks: multimedia codecs, essential repositories, AMD/NVIDIA drivers, graphics acceleration, gaming support (Steam, Heroic, Lutris, Proton), productivity tools, internet apps, audio and video editing, and much more. All with real-time logs and without needing to open the terminal.
00-boas-vindas.sobre_nao_faz_1: It does not replace the terminal — when something goes wrong, some problems still require manual commands for diagnosis.
00-boas-vindas.sobre_nao_faz_2: It does not install games — it prepares the system for you to install and run games, but does not download or install games themselves.
00-boas-vindas.sobre_nao_faz_3: It does not back up your data — we always recommend having snapshots or a backup before making system changes.
00-boas-vindas.sobre_nao_faz_4: It is not affiliated with Red Hat — it is an independent project maintained by the community.
00-boas-vindas.sobre_nao_faz_5: It is not an operating system installer — FOF configures an already-installed Fedora, it does not install Fedora from scratch.
00-boas-vindas.descricao: Before proceeding with the configuration and app installation steps, a complete update of your operating system is highly recommended.
00-boas-vindas.atualizacao_desc: Updates the repository index, synchronizes security keys and downloads the latest versions of all system components.
00-boas-vindas.aviso_reiniciar: 💡 It's recommended to restart your computer after applying system updates, whether directly through the FOF interface or via Fedora's own notification. Restarting ensures that all changes are applied correctly and prevents potential inconsistencies in the system's operation.

01-restauracao.btrfs_desc: Btrfs-Assistant is a graphical tool to manage snapshots of the Btrfs filesystem, allowing you to create and restore backups of your system.
01-restauracao.info_extra: ℹ️ Btrfs-Assistant lets you create snapshots before making changes to the system, ensuring you can restore if something goes wrong.

02-otimizacao.dnf_desc: Configures simultaneous parallel downloads and enables automatic lookup of the fastest server mirror.
02-otimizacao.dnf_info_extra: ℹ️ The setting will be applied with the selected value. You can reapply with different values at any time.
02-otimizacao.idioma_desc: Install translation packages, spell checker, and change the system default locale:
02-otimizacao.idioma_aviso: ⚠️ Note: Restart your computer after completing step 3 to apply the language changes!
02-otimizacao.dual_boot_desc: Makes Fedora use the hardware clock in local time (the same way Windows does by default), fixing the wrong time when switching between systems.
02-otimizacao.dual_boot_aviso: 💡 By default, Windows stores the hardware clock in local time, while Linux (Fedora) stores it in UTC. When you switch between the two, each system interprets the clock differently and the time appears wrong. This button configures Fedora to use local time, matching Windows' behavior — so you don't need to change anything on Windows.
02-otimizacao.dual_boot_confirmar:
⚠️ Adjust the clock to local time?

This will make Fedora use local time (like Windows). The change may cause a temporary jump of a few hours in the clock.

Continue?
02-otimizacao.tuning_desc: Recommended adjustments to improve system responsiveness in games and general use. Each item is independent and can be reverted individually at any time. If you're unsure whether to apply, start with the memory adjustment.
02-otimizacao.vm_max_map_count_titulo: Memory Adjustments for Games and Heavy Applications
02-otimizacao.vm_max_map_count_desc: Increases the maximum number of memory areas each process can map. Fedora's default is 65530, which is insufficient for modern games and heavy applications — several titles fail to launch or crash due to lack of mappable memory (Hogwarts Legacy, Counter-Strike 2, The Finals, Star Citizen, among others).
02-otimizacao.vm_max_map_count_info: ℹ️ What changes: the limit goes from 65,530 to 2,147,483,642 (the practical maximum). It's a compatibility fix, not a "tweak" — the old value causes real failures.
02-otimizacao.vm_swappiness_cache_desc: Adjusts two kernel parameters that control how the system uses swap and file cache. Fedora ships with conservative values that favor the disk; these adjustments make the system keep more RAM available for foreground applications and retain disk caches longer, improving the perceived speed in everyday tasks.
02-otimizacao.vm_swappiness_cache_info:
ℹ️ What changes:
• vm.swappiness: from 60 (default) to 150 — system uses swap more proactively.
• vm.vfs_cache_pressure: from 100 (default) to 50 — kernel retains file caches longer.
Both values are safe for most desktops. If you use an SSD and worry about wear, you can revert later.
02-otimizacao.tcp_bbr_desc: Replaces the default TCP congestion control algorithm (cubic) with BBR, developed by Google. It improves latency and throughput on connections with packet loss, which benefits online gaming, streaming and downloads. It's one of the few network adjustments that bring consistent gains without manual configuration.
02-otimizacao.tcp_bbr_info:
ℹ️ What changes:
• net.core.default_qdisc: from fq_codel to fq (required for BBR).
• net.ipv4.tcp_congestion_control: from cubic to bbr.
No restart required — the effect is immediate after applying.

03-repositorios.descricao: Enables the essential repositories for Fedora: RPM Fusion (packages not included in the official repositories) and Flathub (catalog of Flatpak applications). These repositories are a prerequisite for several of the upcoming sessions.
03-repositorios.rpm_titulo: Enable RPM Fusion Repositories (Free and Non-Free)
03-repositorios.rpm_desc: Installs and synchronizes the official RPM Fusion repositories, adds AppStream metadata support and runs a security adjustment.
03-repositorios.flatpak_desc: Adds the global Flathub repository and ensures the Flatpak package manager is installed on the system.

04-codecs-compatibilidade.descricao: This session brings together everything Fedora needs to handle content that isn't in the official repositories: media codecs (to play videos and audio in any format), commercial DVD playback, and Windows fonts (for compatibility with documents and programs that depend on them).
04-codecs-compatibilidade.codecs_desc: Replaces ffmpeg-free with the full unrestricted version, installs essential gstreamer plugins and enables Cisco OpenH264.
04-codecs-compatibilidade.codecs_info: ℹ️ What this solves: videos in MP4, MKV, AVI, WebM and other formats play in any player (VLC, MPV, Firefox, Chromium). Without these codecs, many files simply won't open or will play without audio/video. It's also a prerequisite for video editing in tools like Kdenlive and Shotcut.
04-codecs-compatibilidade.extras_titulo: Commercial DVD Playback and Additional Firmware
04-codecs-compatibilidade.extras_desc: Enables the restricted sub-repositories (tainted) that bring the libdvdcss library for reading commercial DVDs and proprietary firmware for some hardware.
04-codecs-compatibilidade.extras_info: ℹ️ What this solves: without libdvdcss, Fedora can't read commercial DVDs (with CSS protection) — only homemade DVDs or video files. This item also enables proprietary firmware for some devices that lack a free driver.
04-codecs-compatibilidade.fontes_desc: Installs the Microsoft fonts installer from SourceForge to get Arial, Times, Calibri, etc.
04-codecs-compatibilidade.fontes_aviso: ⚠️ This process downloads and installs proprietary Microsoft fonts. Make sure you comply with the licensing terms.
04-codecs-compatibilidade.fontes_info: ℹ️ Fonts installed: Arial, Times New Roman, Calibri, Cambria, Candara, Consolas, Constantia, Corbel, and others. What this solves: documents in LibreOffice, OnlyOffice and other programs look correct — without these fonts, the system substitutes alternatives that may break the formatting.

05-hardware.descricao: Configuration specific to your hardware: choose the GPU type (AMD or NVIDIA) below to see the corresponding drivers and tools. The controls block is useful for any card.
05-hardware.vulkan_desc: Installs the Vulkan libraries (32-bit and 64-bit), Mesa 3D with the RADV driver (AMD's open-source Vulkan driver), diagnostic tools and compatibility drivers. Essential for Steam, Proton and native games.
05-hardware.vaapi_desc: Hardware video acceleration drivers for smooth playback and encoding. RPM Fusion (Session 4) is a prerequisite for the freeworld version.
05-hardware.vaapi_aviso: 💡 Both buttons install VA-API drivers. The first uses Fedora's default driver; the second applies mesa-va-drivers-freeworld, an alternative for AMD GPUs that don't work with the default. If you're unsure, use the first one.
05-hardware.corectrl_desc: GUI for fan, clock and voltage control on AMD GPUs.
05-hardware.lact_desc: Modern alternative to CoreCtrl for fan, clock and voltage control on AMD GPUs.
05-hardware.overclock_desc: Enables the amdgpu.ppfeaturemask kernel parameter, unlocking advanced clock and voltage adjustments in CoreCtrl and LACT.
05-hardware.overclock_aviso: ⚠️ Requires reboot. Only enable if you know what you're doing — bad overclock can cause instability.
05-hardware.nvidia_aviso: ⚠️ Without nvidia-drm.modeset=1, Wayland is unstable with NVIDIA cards. RPM Fusion (Session 4) is a prerequisite for proprietary drivers. After installing anything here, reboot your computer.
05-hardware.nvidia_driver_desc: Installs akmod-nvidia (recompilable module on every new kernel) and the CUDA + NVENC/NVDEC library extras for OBS, Kdenlive and hardware encoding.
05-hardware.nvidia_modeset_desc: Enables the nvidia-drm.modeset=1 kernel parameter, required for Wayland to work correctly with NVIDIA cards.
05-hardware.input_add_desc: Required for Steam Input, xpadneo and controller drivers to recognize the user. Works for Xbox, PlayStation and Nintendo controllers using kernel drivers.
05-hardware.input_add_aviso: ℹ️ Requires logout/login to take effect.
05-hardware.steam_devices_desc: Installs the udev rules from the steam-devices package, which allow the system to correctly recognize Xbox, PlayStation and Nintendo controllers when used with Steam.
05-hardware.steam_devices_info: ℹ️ What this solves: without these rules, some controllers may not be detected by Steam even when connected. It's a small package that complements the input group above — the group gives your user permission, and this package teaches the system to identify each controller model.

06-gaming.descricao: Installs the main launchers, Windows compatibility tools (Wine/Proton), performance and monitoring utilities, and provides ready-to-use tips to optimize the gaming experience on Fedora.
06-gaming.launchers_desc: Install the main game launchers for Fedora.
06-gaming.launchers_info: ℹ️ All launchers are installed via Flatpak.
06-gaming.compat_desc: Tools to run Windows games and programs outside of Steam, and resources that help with compatibility.
06-gaming.compat_info_extra: ℹ️ Winetricks installs extra components (fonts, libraries) inside a Wine prefix. Bottles is a modern alternative to plain Wine, with visual management of "bottles" (prefixes) and support for Proton-GE runners. NTSYNC is a kernel module that brings significant performance and compatibility improvements for Windows games via Wine/Proton.
06-gaming.ntsync_aviso: ⚠️ What is NTSYNC? It's a Linux kernel module that implements Windows thread synchronization natively in the kernel, reducing CPU overhead and improving game smoothness (fewer micro-stutters and more stable frame times). It's safe to enable — Fedora 44 already enables it by default for Wine/Steam. Recommended for GE-Proton users, where NTSYNC support is already native. The default Wine from repositories does not benefit from NTSYNC yet — in that case, the real gain comes when running games via Proton/GE-Proton. The module will be loaded automatically and will persist between reboots. If a game still doesn't recognize it, restart your computer.
06-gaming.performance_desc: Tools that optimize performance during gameplay and allow monitoring FPS, CPU/GPU usage and other metrics.
06-gaming.performance_info_extra: ℹ️ GameMode sets CPU/GPU to maximum priority while a game is running. MangoHud shows an FPS/CPU/GPU overlay inside the game. Goverlay is a graphical interface to configure MangoHud without editing text files. Gamescope is a Valve micro-compositor that enables upscaling (FSR/NIS), FPS limiting, HDR and more.
06-gaming.gamescope_nvidia_flatpak_aviso: ⚠️ Gamescope + NVIDIA + Flatpak — attention: Gamescope was designed by Valve for the Mesa architecture (AMD/Intel). On NVIDIA cards with the proprietary driver, it can present instability — black screen, frozen cursor or the game closing on open. Additionally, native Gamescope (installed via dnf) has difficulty interacting with games that run inside the Flatpak sandbox, and vice versa. Recommendation: keep everything in the same format. If you use Steam/Heroic via Flatpak, prefer also installing the Flatpak Gamescope extensions; if you use native Steam, prefer native Gamescope. On NVIDIA GPUs, if Gamescope doesn't work well, consider using MangoHud + GameMode as an alternative — they don't have this limitation.
06-gaming.avancado_desc: Tools for those who want to get the most out of Fedora for gaming: specific Proton versions, image post-processing, performance presets and a dedicated gamescope session.
06-gaming.protonup_desc: Graphical interface that downloads and manages Proton-GE versions (community version of Proton, with extra fixes), plus runners for Lutris and Bottles.
06-gaming.protonup_info: ℹ️ After installing, open ProtonUp-Qt, choose the recommended Proton-GE version and click "Download". The latest version usually works well for most games.
06-gaming.vkbasalt_desc: Post-processing layer that adds sharpening, vibrance, FXAA, SMAA and other visual effects directly to Vulkan output. Useful for games that look a bit blurry by default.
06-gaming.vkbasalt_aviso: ⚠️ How to use: after installing, each game needs to enable vkBasalt individually. On Steam, add ENABLE_VKBASALT=1 %command% to the game's launch options. Outside Steam, set the ENABLE_VKBASALT=1 variable before running.
06-gaming.gamemode_presets_desc: Creates ready-to-use config files for MangoHud (FPS overlay) and GameMode (CPU/GPU priority). You get a clean, readable overlay without configuring anything manually.
06-gaming.gamemode_presets_info: ℹ️ Files are created at ~/.config/MangoHud/MangoHud.conf and ~/.config/gamemode.ini. If you already have custom files, they'll be overwritten — back them up beforehand if needed.
06-gaming.gamescope_session_titulo: Gamescope Session — Gaming mode on boot
06-gaming.gamescope_session_desc: Installs an alternative login session that boots the computer directly into Gamescope (the same mode Steam Deck uses). Ideal for HTPCs and TV-connected machines.
06-gaming.gamescope_session_aviso: ⚠️ Note: this is an alternative session — it appears on your display manager's login screen (GDM, SDDM, etc). Your normal session (KDE/GNOME) stays intact. You choose which one to enter at each boot.
06-gaming.controller_test_desc: Installs a graphical tool to test buttons, analog stick dead zones, trigger response and controller rumble. Useful for diagnosing controllers with drift or buttons that don't respond.
06-gaming.emuladores_desc: Emulators for classic and modern consoles on Fedora. All available via Flatpak.
06-gaming.emuladores_aviso_geral: ⚠️ Important notice: some emulators require BIOS, firmware or system files dumped from the original console to work. FOF does not provide these files for legal reasons. Consult each emulator's official documentation for how to obtain them from your own console.
06-gaming.retroarch_desc: Universal emulation frontend that runs dozens of consoles via "cores" (plugins). A single app for SNES, Mega Drive, NES, Game Boy, GBA, PS1 and many others.
06-gaming.retroarch_info: ℹ️ How to install cores: after opening RetroArch, use the Online Updater → Core Downloader menu to download the cores you want (snes9x, genesis_plus_gx, nestopia, mgba, beetle_psx, mupen64plus_next, etc).
06-gaming.dolphin_desc: Mature and very compatible emulator for GameCube and Wii. Runs most games at higher resolution than the original, with upscaling.
06-gaming.pcsx2_desc: PlayStation 2 emulator with upscaling support, widescreen patches and high compatibility with the console's catalog.
06-gaming.pcsx2_aviso: ⚠️ Requires PlayStation 2 BIOS. The BIOS must be dumped from your own console. FOF does not provide this file. After installing, consult the PCSX2 documentation for where to place the BIOS.
06-gaming.rpcs3_desc: PlayStation 3 emulator under active development. Compatibility varies per game — some run perfectly, others still have issues. Check the official compatibility list before installing.
06-gaming.rpcs3_aviso: ⚠️ Requires PlayStation 3 firmware. The firmware must be downloaded from Sony's official website (Sony provides firmware publicly for console updates) and installed by RPCS3 itself. FOF does not download or install this file.
06-gaming.rpcs3_info_extra: ℹ️ About the "unofficial build" notice: RPCS3 may show a message on first run indicating it was installed from an unofficial package. This is a warning from the emulator itself — the Flathub Flatpak is the official distribution channel for RPCS3 on Linux, and the warning does not affect functionality.
06-gaming.duckstation_desc: Modern and lightweight PlayStation 1 emulator, with high resolution support, graphical filters and support for modern controllers. A more user-friendly alternative to the classic ePSXe.
06-gaming.duckstation_aviso: ⚠️ May require PlayStation 1 BIOS. Although Duckstation has a built-in HLE BIOS (works without BIOS for many games), some titles require the real BIOS to function correctly. The BIOS must be dumped from your own console.
06-gaming.rede_desc: Tool to measure your connection quality under load (bufferbloat). The biggest online gaming problem on Linux isn't average ping — it's bufferbloat (ping spikes when the network is being used by other apps).
06-gaming.bufferbloat_desc: Installs a CLI tool that tests your connection quality under load. Measures latency increase when the network is saturated — the famous "ping that spikes out of nowhere" during online games.
06-gaming.bufferbloat_info: ℹ️ The tool used is flent + netperf (RRUL test). After installing, the suggested command is flent rrul -H your-test-server.
06-gaming.bufferbloat_qos_info: ℹ️ About QoS: FOF does not configure QoS automatically because the correct values depend on your specific connection. To configure it, see the bufferbloat.net guide or use tools like flent itself for diagnostics.
06-gaming.bufferbloat_abrir_msg:
To test your connection, open a terminal and run:

flent rrul -H your-test-server

Replace "your-test-server" with the test host.

You can use public servers like:
  flent rrul -H flent-public.bufferbloat.net
06-gaming.anticheat_desc: Informational panel about which anti-cheats work on Linux, which don't, and why. Nothing here is installed or executed — it's just for you to know before buying or trying a game.
06-gaming.dicas_desc: Recommended settings to get the most out of games on Fedora.
06-gaming.dicas_aviso_steam: 💡 Steam — Launch Options: you can add commands to each game's launch options (right-click the game → Properties → Launch Options). Examples:
06-gaming.dicas_nota: ℹ️ Replace the -W and -H values with the desired resolution. -r 60 limits FPS to 60 — remove it if you want unlimited FPS.

07-loja.descricao: Tools to record, edit, stream and produce audio and video content on Fedora.
07-loja.obs_titulo: 🎬 OBS Studio - Installation and Virtual Camera
07-loja.obs_desc: Install OBS Studio for recording/streaming and enable the virtual camera for video calls.
07-loja.obs_aviso: ⚠️ The virtual camera requires Secure Boot to be configured correctly or disabled.
07-loja.easyeffects_desc: Sound effects processor for PipeWire to apply noise reduction and equalization.
07-loja.audio_tuning_desc: Adjustments that improve the experience for those who record, produce or game with real-time audio. Each item is independent and can be reverted individually. Recommended for users of tools like Ardour, LMMS, Reaper or those who stream with live monitoring.
07-loja.realtime_setup_desc: Configures the system to allow audio applications (Ardour, LMMS, Reaper, Jack) to have real-time priority. Without this, audio can present glitches (crackling or xruns) under load, even with ample hardware. The adjustment installs Fedora's official realtime-setup package and adds your user to the realtime group.
07-loja.realtime_setup_info:
ℹ️ What changes:
• realtime group created and configured with adequate memory limits.
• Your user added to this group — requires logout/login to take effect.
• Limit configuration files installed by Fedora's official package.
07-loja.realtime_setup_aviso: ⚠️ Requires logout/login: the realtime group only takes effect after you log out and back in. Without this, applications continue running with default priority — even with the adjustment applied.
07-loja.pipewire_quantum_desc: Reduces the PipeWire quantum (audio buffer size) from 1024 to 256 samples. This reduces audio latency from ~21ms to ~5ms, making live monitoring and real-time playback more responsive — essential for recording and games with positional audio.
07-loja.pipewire_quantum_info:
ℹ️ What changes:
• Creates the file ~/.config/pipewire/pipewire.conf.d/99-fof-quantum.conf.
• Restarts the user services pipewire, pipewire-pulse and wireplumber.
• Applies immediately — no system reboot required.
• Trade-off: lower latency uses slightly more CPU. On modest machines, it can cause crackling under heavy load. If that happens, revert.
07-loja.streaming_desc: Tools for live streamers: OBS scene templates, Streamdeck integration, NDI and more.
07-loja.obs_scene_desc: Creates a set of default scenes in OBS Studio (Intro, Gameplay, Just Chatting, BRB, Ending) so you only need to customize details later.
07-loja.obs_scene_aviso: ⚠️ Templates are created in ~/.config/obs-studio/. If you already have custom scenes, they'll be preserved — templates are added in a separate collection.
07-loja.streamdeck_desc: Graphical interface to control the Elgato Streamdeck on Linux, open-source alternative to the official software (which has no Linux version).
07-loja.ndi_desc: Network Device Interface protocol. Allows transmitting video between computers, widely used in multi-PC streaming setups.
07-loja.pipewire_desc: Visual audio routing with PipeWire. Lets you separate each application's sound (game, mic, Discord, browser) into distinct tracks — ideal for streaming, where you want OBS to record everything, but Discord to only hear the microphone.
07-loja.qpwgraph_desc: Graphical interface to view and connect PipeWire audio tracks. You drag a connection to enable/disable routing between applications.
07-loja.qpwgraph_info: ℹ️ After installing, open qpwgraph and you'll see a diagram with all applications and audio devices connected. Drag a line to create a connection, or right-click a line to remove it.
07-loja.presets_desc: Ready-to-use templates for video transcoding (HandBrake) and Kdenlive projects, to save time.
07-loja.handbrake_desc: Open-source video transcoder. We install it with ready-to-use presets for YouTube (1080p60), storage (H.265) and social media (vertical).
07-loja.handbrake_info: ℹ️ After installing, open HandBrake and go to Presets → Import to load the FOF presets. They're stored at ~/.config/ghb/presets.json.
07-loja.kdenlive_templates_desc: Creates Kdenlive project files ready for 1080p60, 4K30 and vertical (Shorts/Reels/TikTok). You open it and start editing right away.
07-loja.kdenlive_templates_info: ℹ️ Templates are saved at ~/Videos/Kdenlive-Templates/. Open them in Kdenlive via File → Open.
07-loja.captura_desc: Tool to record the screen with one click, with a ready quality preset.
07-loja.screen_recorder_desc: Installs the native screen recorder (wf-recorder on Wayland, SimpleScreenRecorder on X11), with a shortcut configured. Videos go to ~/Videos.
07-loja.screen_recorder_aviso: ⚠️ On Wayland, screen recording may require confirmation from the compositor (system window asking for permission). It's a Wayland security feature.

08-waydroid.aviso_nvidia: ⚠️ Waydroid requires AMD or Intel GPU. Users with NVIDIA GPU cannot use this session (the proprietary driver doesn't expose the required Mesa). There's an experimental project (waydroid-nvidia) that tries to work around it via Vulkan proxy, but it's not supported by FOF.
08-waydroid.descricao: Waydroid runs Android inside a container on Fedora. This session installs Waydroid, initializes the container with the Android image, and offers the most requested extras (Google Play Store, ARM translation, Magisk, Widevine).
08-waydroid.waydroid_desc: Installs Waydroid and lzip (dependency for the extras script). We use the COPR yanqiyu/waydroid because the official package is broken on Fedora 44 (Bug 2420131) and the COPR has the working version for Fedora 44/45.
08-waydroid.init_desc: Downloads the Android images (system ~1.2 GB + vendor ~190 MB) and initializes the container. Uses the GAPPS variant (with Google Apps). Runs once — after that, use "Open Waydroid" to start the container whenever you want.
08-waydroid.open_desc: Opens the Android interface. Starts the container if it's not running. The container must be running to install extras (GApps, Magisk, etc.). Click here once before using the extras.
08-waydroid.uninstall_desc: Removes Waydroid and all container data (images, installed Android apps, settings). Irreversible action.
08-waydroid.confirmar_uninstall: This will remove Waydroid and ALL Android container data (installed apps, settings). Continue?
08-waydroid.prep_desc: Clones waydroid_script, creates an isolated Python environment (venv) and installs dependencies. This step is a prerequisite for all extras below. Runs once.
08-waydroid.prep_aviso: ⚠️ Requires Waydroid to be installed, initialized AND with the container running (use "Open Waydroid" above). Without that, the extras fail.
08-waydroid.gapps_desc: Installs Google apps, including the Google Play Store, in the Android container. Requires the Extras Environment to be prepared and the container running.
08-waydroid.arm_desc: Allows running Android apps compiled for ARM on x86_64 machines. libndk usually has better performance on AMD CPUs; libhoudini is the traditional option for Intel. Install only one of them.
08-waydroid.magisk_desc: Advanced suite for Android users. Provides root and module management inside the container. Requires the Extras Environment to be prepared.
08-waydroid.widevine_desc: DRM L3 support for services like Netflix, Spotify and other streaming inside the Android container. Requires the Extras Environment to be prepared.
08-waydroid.smartdock_desc: Support for Logitech SmartDock hardware. Requires the Extras Environment to be prepared.
08-waydroid.helper_desc: GUI for advanced Waydroid configuration. Installation via the official COPR cuteneko/waydroid-helper.
08-waydroid.prefs_desc: Applies tweaks that improve usability (independent windows, proper DPI, touch behavior in games).
08-waydroid.prefs_aviso: ⚠️ The Waydroid container must be running for these settings to apply. Open Waydroid once before using this button.
08-waydroid.container_running: Waydroid container is running. You can install the extras.
08-waydroid.container_stopped: Waydroid container is not running. Click "Open Waydroid" in the section above before using the extras.
08-waydroid.container_not_ready: Waydroid is not installed or initialized yet. Follow the steps in the section above first.
08-waydroid.container_waiting: Waiting for the container to come up (up to 3 minutes)...
08-waydroid.container_timeout: Container did not respond within 3 minutes. Check /tmp/fof-waydroid-ui.log for details.
08-waydroid.container_guard_alert: Waydroid container is not running. Click "Open Waydroid" first.

09-softwares-uteis.bloco1_desc: Tools to work with documents, notes, email and e-books.
09-softwares-uteis.bloco2_desc: Video, music and streaming players to consume content day to day.
09-softwares-uteis.bloco3_desc: Image editing, vector illustration, 3D modeling, CAD and 3D printing.
09-softwares-uteis.bloco4_desc: Browsers, video call apps and messengers.
09-softwares-uteis.bloco5_desc: Video editors, 3D modeling, audio editing and music production.
09-softwares-uteis.bloco6_desc: Tools to sync files with Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox and other services.
09-softwares-uteis.affinity_desc: Affinity has no native Linux version. This button opens the AffinityOnLinux installer, a community project (not affiliated with Serif/Canva) that sets up a pre-configured Wine environment to run Affinity.
09-softwares-uteis.affinity_aviso: ⚠️ You must have purchased and downloaded the Affinity .exe installer from the official Serif/Canva website before using this — FOF only prepares the Wine environment and opens the community installer; that installer will ask for the .exe file at the right moment. It's a third-party project: if something doesn't work on your hardware, check their known issues page.
09-softwares-uteis.affinity_prereq: 📦 Prerequisite: PyQt6 is required for the installer interface. FOF checks and installs it automatically if needed.
09-softwares-uteis.lightworks_aviso: ⚠️ Note: Lightworks is not installed via Flatpak. The button downloads the RPM package directly from the official LWKS website. Updates are not automatic — to update, run this button again.
09-softwares-uteis.rclone_aviso: ℹ️ Cloud account setup: Rclone Manager is a graphical interface for Rclone. It lets you configure access to Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, S3, and dozens of other cloud storage services. After installing both apps, open Rclone Manager and follow the guide inside its interface to add your accounts. FOF only installs the tools — setting up the accounts is done by you, inside Rclone Manager.

10-casa-pronta.descricao: Settings to get Fedora ready for home use: printer, file sharing with Windows/phone, password manager and PDF reading with OCR. All in independent blocks — use only what you need.
10-casa-pronta.cups_desc: Installs Fedora's printing system (CUPS), support for automatic network printer discovery (Avahi/Bonjour) and generic drivers. After installing, most modern printers are recognized automatically in Settings → Printers.
10-casa-pronta.cups_info: ℹ️ What is installed: cups, avahi (network discovery), system-config-printer (management GUI) and ghostscript (format conversion). The CUPS service is enabled automatically.
10-casa-pronta.cups_info_drivers: ℹ️ About specific drivers: HP printers may need hplip, Brother needs brother-* (from the manufacturer's site), Epson needs epson-inkjet-printer-escpr. After installing CUPS, open Printer Settings — the system suggests the missing drivers.
10-casa-pronta.compart_desc: Tools to transfer and share files between Fedora and other devices. Choose according to your case: Windows on the local network (Samba), Android/iPhone (LocalSend) or Linux network (Warpinator).
10-casa-pronta.samba_desc: Installs Samba, which allows sharing Fedora folders with Windows computers on the same network — and also accessing Windows shared folders from Fedora.
10-casa-pronta.samba_aviso: ⚠️ After installing: open Nautilus/Dolphin, right-click a folder → Properties → Sharing (or Folder Sharing) and check "Share this folder". Fedora takes care of the rest.
10-casa-pronta.samba_info: ℹ️ What is installed: samba, samba-client and cifs-utils (to mount Windows folders). The smb and nmb services are enabled.
10-casa-pronta.localsend_desc: Cross-platform app (Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS) that sends files between devices on the same local network. It's the modern alternative to AirDrop — works across any combination of systems, with a simple interface.
10-casa-pronta.localsend_info: ℹ️ How to use: install LocalSend on Fedora (via FOF) and on your phone (via app store). Open both on the same Wi-Fi network, and the devices find each other automatically. No account, no cloud, no ads.
10-casa-pronta.warpinator_desc: File transfer tool from Linux Mint, available for Fedora. Simple and direct: open it, it finds other Warpinator devices on the network and transfers files with one click. Ideal if you have more than one Linux at home.
10-casa-pronta.warpinator_info: ℹ️ When to use: if the destination is also Linux, Warpinator is often faster than LocalSend (less overhead). For phone, use LocalSend.
10-casa-pronta.keepassxc_desc: Local, open-source, cloud-free password manager. Stores everything in an encrypted .kdbx file on your computer — you decide if you sync it (via Nextcloud, Syncthing, USB drive, etc). Integrates with browsers and supports autofill.
10-casa-pronta.keepassxc_info: ℹ️ Why KeePassXC instead of Bitwarden? KeePassXC is 100% offline and local — nothing leaves your computer. Ideal for those who prefer not to depend on any service. If you prefer cloud convenience, Bitwarden is also a good option (but FOF installs KeePassXC, which is more aligned with the local-first philosophy).
10-casa-pronta.okular_tesseract_titulo: Okular + Tesseract — PDF Reader with OCR
10-casa-pronta.okular_tesseract_desc: Installs Okular (PDF, e-book and comic reader, very fast) and Tesseract (OCR engine). With both, you can open a scanned PDF (image) and extract the text — useful for copying excerpts from scanned documents.
10-casa-pronta.okular_tesseract_info: ℹ️ What is OCR: Optical Character Recognition — converts text images (scanned, photographed) into searchable and copyable text. Tesseract supports Portuguese, English and 100+ languages. In Okular, use Tools → Text Selection on scanned PDFs (with Tesseract installed, it recognizes automatically).
10-casa-pronta.okular_tesseract_info_lang: ℹ️ Additional OCR languages: we install the base package with Portuguese and English. If you need another language, look for tesseract-langpack-XX in Discover/GNOME Software.

11-diagnostico.descricao: Visual panel of system state. Shows in real time what's happening with CPU, memory, disk and services — without needing to open the terminal. Useful for investigating slowness, disk usage, temperature and recent errors.
11-diagnostico.aviso_geral: ℹ️ This panel is read-only. No command here changes the system — they're all queries. If you want to fix something specific, the actions are in the other FOF sessions.
11-diagnostico.painel_desc: Data collected from FOF's local endpoints. Some values update automatically; others can be updated manually.
11-diagnostico.top5_desc: Processes consuming the most CPU and memory right now.
11-diagnostico.otimizacoes_desc: Shows the current state of the performance tunings that can be applied in the Optimization session (session 02) and Media Production session (session 07). Values in green indicate the tuning is active; neutral values indicate Fedora's default. This section is informational only — to apply or revert a tuning, use the buttons in the corresponding sessions.
11-diagnostico.otimizacoes_info: ℹ️ About the values: this section only shows what's currently active. Each tuning is reversible and can be applied or reverted individually in sessions 02 (Optimization) and 07 (Media Production). If a tuning is blank or shows "N/A", the feature may not be available on this kernel — it's not an error.
11-diagnostico.armazen_desc: See how much space each partition is using and where the largest files are. Useful when the system warns "disk full" or when you don't know what's eating up space.
11-diagnostico.particoes_desc: Lists mounted partitions with usage, free space and mount point.
11-diagnostico.baobab_desc: Installs Baobab (Disk Usage Analyzer), which shows a visual map of where your disk space is — much easier than trying to figure it out yourself.
11-diagnostico.baobab_info: ℹ️ How to use: after installing, open it from the application menu (search for "Disk Usage Analyzer" or "Baobab"), point it at the disk or folder you want to analyze, and it shows a tree diagram with the largest files.
11-diagnostico.saude_desc: Disk health check (HDDs and SSDs) via SMART and reading component temperatures (CPU, GPU, motherboard). Helps detect problems before they become serious failure.
11-diagnostico.gsmart_desc: Installs GSmartControl, a graphical interface for smartctl. It shows disk health, temperature, hours of use, bad sectors, and allows running quick and extended tests with a click.
11-diagnostico.gsmart_info: ℹ️ How to interpret: in the "Health" column, a green ✅ means a healthy disk. A red ❌ means failure — back up immediately. Temperatures above 55°C under continuous use deserve attention.
11-diagnostico.gsmart_info_root: ℹ️ About the password: when opening GSmartControl, it may ask for administrator password to read SMART data — this is normal (the smartctl needs access to the physical device). The password window comes from the system, not from FOF.
11-diagnostico.coolercontrol_desc: Installs CoolerControl, a complete monitoring and thermal control center. In addition to showing temperatures, fan speeds and other sensors in real time, it lets you create custom fan curves (for example, "when the GPU reaches 60°C, spin the fan at 50%"). It's the most robust and official thermal management tool on Fedora.
11-diagnostico.coolercontrol_info:
ℹ️ What you can do with it:
  • View temperatures of CPU, GPU and motherboard in real time
  • View speed (RPM) of all system fans
  • Create custom fan curves based on any sensor
  • Configure alerts for high temperatures or fan failures
  • Build dashboards with the data you use the most
11-diagnostico.coolercontrol_info_copr: ℹ️ About installation: CoolerControl is not in Fedora's standard repositories. We use the project's official COPR (codifryed/CoolerControl), maintained by the developer himself.
11-diagnostico.coolercontrol_info_group: ℹ️ About permissions: FOF adds your user to the coolercontrol group so the GUI can control fans without asking for a password on every action. That group only takes effect after logging out and back in. The daemon starts working immediately.
11-diagnostico.coolercontrol_info_sensors: ℹ️ If a sensor doesn't appear: CoolerControl uses the same sensors as lm_sensors. If a sensor is missing, open the terminal and run sudo sensors-detect, answering "YES" to all questions. Then restart the service: sudo systemctl restart coolercontrold.
11-diagnostico.journal_desc: Filters the systemd journal for error messages from the last 24 hours and groups them by origin — so you quickly see if something is failing repeatedly without having to read the raw log.
11-diagnostico.journal_info: ℹ️ Important: not every error in the journal is a problem. Services that try to start before the hardware is ready, or drivers that report warnings during boot, are normal. Use this panel to detect patterns: the same error appearing dozens of times indicates something that needs attention.

12-fedora.descricao: Fedora-specific information and tools: installed version check, Fedora Atomic/Silverblue (immutable systems) detection and SELinux management — Fedora's mandatory security system, often poorly understood by those coming from other distributions.
12-fedora.aviso_geral: ℹ️ This session is informative. Commands here only read system state. Nothing is changed without you explicitly clicking a button — and the ones that do change make clear what they do.
12-fedora.versao_desc: FOF is developed and tested on Fedora 44. If you're on a different version, some commands may behave unexpectedly (renamed packages, changed repositories, new syntax). This check warns you when that happens.
12-fedora.versao_info: ℹ️ Supported versions: Fedora 43, 44 and 45. Older versions (42 and earlier) or newer (46+) may require manual adjustments. FOF keeps working, but you may need to adapt a specific command.
12-fedora.atomic_desc: Fedora has two variants: "traditional" (Workstation, KDE, etc) and "immutable" (Silverblue, Kinoite, Bazzite, Bluefin). On immutable variants, the base system is protected and cannot be modified by dnf install — only by rpm-ostree or bootc.
12-fedora.atomic_info: ℹ️ Why this matters: FOF uses dnf to install most packages. If you're on an immutable system, those commands will fail (or worse, require override). This detection warns you before you try something that won't work.
12-fedora.selinux_desc: SELinux is Fedora's mandatory access control system. It enforces strict rules about what each process can do — even processes running as root are limited. It's Fedora's biggest mystery for those coming from other distributions, and the most common cause of "why doesn't this work?".
12-fedora.selinux_status_desc: Shows the current SELinux mode (enforcing, permissive or disabled).
12-fedora.selinux_status_info:
ℹ️ SELinux modes:
  • Enforcing — rules active and real blocks. It's Fedora's default and recommended mode.
  • Permissive — rules active but only logs, doesn't block. Good for diagnosing.
  • Disabled — rules deactivated. Not recommended — reduces system security.
12-fedora.selinux_trouble_desc: Lists "AVC denial" warnings from the last 24 hours. Each AVC is an access attempt that SELinux blocked. Not every block is a problem — many are noise from processes trying to access things outside the policy, but the pattern helps identify real problems.
12-fedora.selinux_trouble_info: ℹ️ How to interpret: an isolated AVC is usually harmless. Multiple repeated AVCs from the same process indicate it's trying something SELinux doesn't allow — that deserves investigation.
12-fedora.setroubleshoot_desc: Installs setroubleshoot, an official Fedora package that automatically analyzes each AVC and suggests a fix — in plain language, without SELinux jargon. It's what turns "usuário_u:role_r:tipo_t" into "Apache cannot read files in /var/www/html, you should run such command".
12-fedora.setroubleshoot_info: ℹ️ What is installed: setroubleshoot-server (analysis engine), setools-console (CLI tools) and policycoreutils-python-utils (policy utilities). Warnings appear automatically in the desktop notification menu when an AVC is generated.
12-fedora.selinux_gui_desc: Installs policycoreutils-gui, which provides a complete graphical interface to manage SELinux: booleans, file contexts, port mapping, users, and other advanced settings. It's the friendliest way to view and adjust SELinux on Fedora.
12-fedora.selinux_gui_info:
ℹ️ What you can do with it:
  • View and toggle booleans (feature on/off switches)
  • View file contexts (what each folder can access)
  • Configure allowed ports for each service
  • Manage SELinux users
12-fedora.selinux_gui_info_root: ℹ️ About the password: when opening the SELinux Manager, it will ask for administrator password — this is normal. Without root, it only allows viewing; to change things, privilege is required.
12-fedora.selinux_desabilitar_desc: Many tutorials on the internet recommend disabling SELinux when something doesn't work. This is not a good practice on Fedora — the system is designed to work with it enabled, and disabling masks problems instead of solving them.
12-fedora.selinux_desabilitar_info: ℹ️ If you need to change the mode: the official tool is setenforce. Running sudo setenforce 0 sets it to permissive until the next boot. To make it permanent, edit /etc/selinux/config (we don't do this automatically — it's your decision).
